newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds seen falling further after German Ifo.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds seen falling further after German Ifo.

text.p: Danish bond prices fell on Tuesday following Germany down after the Ifo institute said European central banks were under pressure to raise rates to defend currencies with dealers expecting more falls ahead.

"The rather negative Ifo-index combined with persistent uncertainty about the German repo rate possibly being made variable, has created a certain amount of uncertainty in the market so we can expect more falls," one dealer said.
The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was down 0.49 point from the opening at 112.71, yielding 6.05 percent at 1140 GMT.R

The upcoming seven percent 2007 benchmark was 0.51 point lower at 105.61, with the yield at 6.23 percent. Turnover in the tone-setting 2006 and 2007 bonds was 1.9 billion and 900 million crowns respectively.

The 2006's September future fell 0.58 point to 112.10 with 53 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 lost 1.20 point to 91.48. The crown traded at 3.8108 per mark, up a tad from around 3.8110 at the opening.
The 2007's 10-year yield gap with Germany was unchanged at 54 basis points.
